title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned House Lights. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: House Lights
options.lineage: the auditorium itself: velvet, proscenium, follow-spot, intertitle cards
options.thesis: Pausing brings the house lights up: the room around the screen appears and the character steps down from the frame into the front row.
options.viewport: Held frame left, slightly dimmed with a follow-spot still on the chosen face; right, the front row in claret velvet: full-bleed portrait, name in tall marquee caps, the conversation set as intertitles and lines.
options.risk: A dark cinema is the obvious reading of a movie product; it only escapes the default if the velvet colour truly carries the room and the house-lights motion is built, not implied.

raised.raise: Every reply sentence is visible before it sounds: dim while its spoiler check runs, lit the instant its audio starts.
System states print themselves as intertitle cards in the conversation (Recognising faces, It is 1943 for him) instead of badges and chrome.
House-light gold is reserved for what is live right now (the character speaking, your mic recording) and appears nowhere else.
Recognised faces wear a dashed follow-spot; only the chosen one goes solid.
The character's portrait owns its card full-bleed, with a name lockup that still reads at chip size.
The mechanism reads in half a second: a strip with the lived part of the film lit and the rest dark, labelled not yet.

options.label: Revision Pages
options.lineage: production screenplays and their coloured revision pages
options.thesis: Your conversation is typed into the film's screenplay as a new scene, on the next colour of revision page.
options.viewport: The held frame becomes a slugline (INT. LOS ALAMOS – 1943); below it a page in revision blue where the character's cue is centred and dialogue lands line by line as it is spoken.
options.risk: Screenplay-as-chat is a known movie trope, and the page can drift toward the cream-paper default if the revision colours are timid.

options.label: Algorave Source Floor
options.lineage: live-coded music projected on a club wall
options.thesis: The character's reply as live code the room can watch before it plays.
options.viewport: A stage-scale code buffer with the next spoken line flashing before it sounds.
options.case: Fuses poorly: film viewers and judges don't recognise themselves in a code buffer, and it hides the film.
options.kept: Show what is about to be spoken before it sounds.
options.risk: Reads as a developer toy, not a film.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The conversation as one glowing transcript where states print themselves.
options.viewport: An 80-column transcript with a breathing cursor beside the frozen frame.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a tool costume with no tie to cinema; loses identification and clarity.
options.kept: System states print themselves in the transcript instead of chrome.

options.label: Raku Smoke Flash
options.thesis: Soot-black ground, crackled silver body, ember only on the live vessel.
options.viewport: The character's portrait as a fired vessel, ember-lit while speaking.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in the film-viewing world connects to ceramics.
options.kept: One hot colour reserved strictly for the live thing.

options.label: Sewing Pattern Envelope
options.thesis: Characters as lettered views; the chosen one cut solid, the rest dashed.
options.viewport: The paused frame with dashed cutting lines around each face.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a craft world foreign to film; the picker metaphor is clever but obscures the product.

options.label: Skate Deck Wall
options.thesis: Characters as tall full-bleed decks you pull off the rack and flip.
options.viewport: A rack of tall character cards; the pulled one flips to the conversation.
options.case: Fuses poorly: loud and fun, but the film disappears and judges read merch, not story.
options.kept: Portrait full-bleed, name lockup legible at small size.

options.label: Fletcher Wit Poster
options.thesis: One visual pun explains the product before the words do.
options.viewport: A cut-paper character with a torn-off future.
options.case: Fuses poorly: charming, but the light paper world fights watching a film in a dark room.
options.kept: The idea legible in half a second.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A streaming-app player with an X-Ray style side panel, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Player left, a dark chat sidebar right with a round avatar and message bubbles.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every streaming companion app by design.
